D1 research authoring, batch 81 (2026-09-27): three ASSOCIATION_ONLY draft mappings added at ranks 1, 2, and 3 (dysphagia, depressive-disorder, xerostomia) pending qualified-human citation verification under docs/citation-verification-sop.md; mapping approval is not citation verification. The target identities dysphagia, depressive-disorder, and xerostomia all had zero registered salivary-gland incoming edges before this batch, and xerostomia had no registered edge of any kind.

Classification guard: all three edges assert association only (etiologicalConsensus NOT_ESTABLISHED, vaNexusProbabilityAlignment NOT_ASSERTED, hypothesizedOnly:true) at three different mechanism categories, MECHANICAL_OR_COMPRESSIVE for dysphagia, PSYCHOPHYSIOLOGICAL for depression, and POST_SURGICAL_OR_TREATMENT for xerostomia. The xerostomia mechanism deliberately splits a documented vector from a hypothesized one within a single field, because the located evidence documents radiation-induced acinar secretory loss while the tumour-infiltration and resection route has no located anchor. The mood edge states plainly that its only direct anchor reports a PHQ-8 screening prevalence rather than a diagnosed-disorder rate, and that the oropharyngeal systematic review contains NO mood data and is registered as disease-trajectory context only.

Withheld routes and duplicate-scope screen: no facial-nerve-palsy edge (MISSING IDENTITY - the most frequent neurological accompaniment of parotid malignancy has no catalog identity); no hearing-loss edge (EVIDENCE-INSUFFICIENT - the located parotid literature reports facial nerve schwannoma and lateral skull base invasion rather than a quantified hearing-loss association, and the nine registered hearing-loss sources are all otologic or neurologic, none oncologic); no anxiety-disorder edge (TARGET-EXHAUSTION - the same cohort reports GAD-7 elevation at 7.1 percent, below the threshold at which a separate edge would add information the depression edge does not carry); and no insomnia edge despite a 7.2 percent prevalence in the same cohort, on the same target-exhaustion basis. Note for the reviewer that PMID 38905553 was already registered in the master source registry before this batch, so the xerostomia edge reuses it as an additional reference use rather than creating a duplicate source entity.

nexusClaim.associationBasis: Dysphagia is the best-quantified symptomatic burden in the located malignant parotid cohort and is documented as a presenting symptom across independent salivary-gland carcinoma sites: a survivorship-clinic retrospective study of 62 surgically treated malignant parotid tumour patients reports clinically relevant dysphagia symptoms on the Eating Assessment Tool in 32.3 percent at last follow-up, with patients treated with surgery plus adjuvant chemoradiation having significantly worse swallowing scores than those treated with surgery alone (p=0.03) and patients treated with surgery plus adjuvant radiotherapy having significantly worse physical and social-emotional quality of life than surgery alone (p<0.01 and p=0.01 respectively) (PMID 38837232); a PRISMA systematic review of 44 articles covering 195 patients with oropharyngeal adenoid cystic carcinoma reports presenting symptoms to be mainly pain or discomfort (n=31) followed by a palpable mass (n=19) and dysphagia (n=12), with the base of tongue the most common subsite at 73 percent, positive cervical nodes in 22.3 percent at diagnosis, and distant metastases in 36 percent of those who progressed, primarily to the lungs (n=26) (PMID 42371638); and a dedicated analysis of 29 cases of malignant salivary gland tumours of the tongue confirms that tongue subsite is a recognised and separately reported presentation category (PMID 41793734); recorded as documented association only, with the treatment gradient carried as an explicit confounder rather than as evidence of tumour-driven dysphagia alone.
nexusClaim.causationStatus: Neither causation nor aggravation of dysphagia is established for any individual, and the located cohort is explicit that treatment is a co-driver: the 32.3 percent dysphagia figure is a survivorship-clinic prevalence at last follow-up in patients who had already undergone surgery, and the same cohort reports that the dysphagia difference is significant between surgery plus chemoradiation and surgery alone, which means the measured burden is at least partly iatrogenic and cannot be attributed to the tumour; base-of-tongue and oral-cavity subsites are mechanically obstructive by anatomy rather than by disease mechanism, so a mass at that subsite produces dysphagia through physical obstruction of the swallowing lumen and a base-of-tongue adenoid cystic carcinoma is a different clinical entity from a parotid malignancy even though both are salivary gland carcinoma; the systematic review is a synthesis of 44 small studies with 195 total patients and no pooled estimate, so its counts describe a literature rather than a population; and none of the three anchors separates dysphagia caused by the primary tumour from dysphagia caused by surgery, radiation-induced fibrosis, neck dissection, xerostomia-induced dentition change, or a distant metastasis, all of which are plausible in this population. Individual claims require a dated dysphagia assessment with an instrumental or validated clinical measure, documented tumour subsite and stage, a dated treatment timeline separating pre-treatment from post-treatment swallowing status, and exclusion of post-surgical stricture, radiation fibrosis, and metastatic obstruction.

causalMechanism.primaryVector: The hypothesised vector is physical obstruction of the swallowing lumen by a primary tumour at a base-of-tongue, oral-cavity, or oropharyngeal salivary subsite, compounded rather than replaced by a second treatment-mediated vector in which surgical resection, neck dissection, and radiation-induced fibrosis reduce pharyngeal compliance and salivary lubrication; the mechanical vector predominates where the primary subsite is oral or pharyngeal and the treatment vector predominates where the primary is a minor salivary gland of the parotid or submandibular region treated with radiotherapy to fields that include the pharynx, and which vector dominates in any individual depends entirely on subsite and treatment, which is the specific reason the edge is held at association only.

evidentiaryProfile.conservativeRationale: Authored at ASSOCIATION_ONLY at survivorship-retrospective, PRISMA-systematic-review, and case-series class following the file's existing oncologic and treatment-related pathway scope: the survivorship anchor is the only located design with a patient-reported dysphagia instrument and the only one that reports a treatment gradient, and it is registered together with that gradient rather than with the prevalence figure alone, because the gradient is the finding that discloses the iatrogenic component (PMID 38837232); the systematic review supplies the subsite distribution and the presenting-symptom profile that make the mechanical vector concrete, and it is the anchor that shows the presenting symptom count for dysphagia is small relative to pain and mass (PMID 42371638); the tongue case series confirms the subsite-specific literature exists as a separate body rather than as an extrapolation (PMID 41793734). Because the design cannot separate tumour-driven from treatment-driven dysphagia, the conservative standard keeps the edge at association only, names both vectors in the mechanism, and routes individual attribution through subsite, stage, and a dated pre-treatment versus post-treatment swallowing comparison.
evidentiaryProfile.evidenceGaps: All three anchors are observational or synthesis designs and none separates tumour from treatment as the driver; the survivorship anchor is a single multidisciplinary clinic with 62 patients and a level-4 evidence designation self-reported by the authors, and it reports prevalence at last follow-up rather than at diagnosis, so it cannot establish when the dysphagia began; its dysphagia comparison across treatment groups is significant at p=0.03 in a cohort of 62 with three treatment strata, which is a fragile threshold; the systematic review includes 44 articles but only 195 patients, meaning the pooled literature is composed of very small series with substantial selection bias, and it reports raw symptom counts without denominators by subsite; the tongue case series of 29 cases is single-institutional; no located anchor reports instrumental swallow study results, aspiration events, or nutrition status; and no anchor reports how many dysphagia cases were attributable to radiation-induced xerostomia compounding the mechanical obstruction, which is the interaction the present batch documents separately at the xerostomia edge. Facial nerve palsy, the most frequent neurological accompaniment of parotid malignancy, was reviewed and withheld as MISSING IDENTITY because no facial-nerve-palsy identity exists in the catalog.
alternativeEtiologiesToRuleOut: Dysphagia arising from radiation-induced fibrosis, neck dissection, or post-surgical stricture rather than from the primary tumour
Dysphagia from a distant metastasis, most commonly pulmonary, or from a synchronous second primary
Xerostomia-induced dentition and mucosal change compounding mechanical obstruction, documented separately at this file's rank 3 edge
Presurgical dysphagia from a pre-existing swallowing disorder or prior head and neck surgery

evidenceGaps: All three anchors are observational or synthesis designs and none separates tumour from treatment as the driver; the survivorship anchor is a single multidisciplinary clinic with 62 patients and a level-4 evidence designation self-reported by the authors, and it reports prevalence at last follow-up rather than at diagnosis, so it cannot establish when the dysphagia began; its dysphagia comparison across treatment groups is significant at p=0.03 in a cohort of 62 with three treatment strata, which is a fragile threshold; the systematic review includes 44 articles but only 195 patients, meaning the pooled literature is composed of very small series with substantial selection bias, and it reports raw symptom counts without denominators by subsite; the tongue case series of 29 cases is single-institutional; no located anchor reports instrumental swallow study results, aspiration events, or nutrition status; and no anchor reports how many dysphagia cases were attributable to radiation-induced xerostomia compounding the mechanical obstruction, which is the interaction the present batch documents separately at the xerostomia edge. Facial nerve palsy, the most frequent neurological accompaniment of parotid malignancy, was reviewed and withheld as MISSING IDENTITY because no facial-nerve-palsy identity exists in the catalog.
suggestions.rationale: Authoring registers this edge because dysphagia is the single most frequently measured symptomatic burden in the located malignant parotid cohort at 32.3 percent, because it is the complication a benefits examiner is most likely to encounter in a salivary gland carcinoma survivor, and because the target identity is heavily used with sixteen registered incoming edges yet has no salivary-gland primary. The conservative framing registers the treatment gradient as the finding that discloses the iatrogenic component rather than burying it, names mechanical obstruction and treatment fibrosis as two separable vectors whose relative weight depends on subsite, and requires a dated pre-treatment versus post-treatment swallowing comparison before any individual attribution.

nexusClaim.associationBasis: Depressive symptoms are measured directly in the located malignant parotid survivorship cohort and are reported to worsen with adjuvant treatment, which makes this the one emotional-burden edge in this file supported by an instrument rather than inferred: the same 62-patient cohort reports elevated depressive symptoms on the PHQ-8 in 15.5 percent at last follow-up, alongside social-emotional quality of life significantly worse in patients who received adjuvant radiotherapy (p=0.01) and adjuvant chemoradiotherapy (p=0.02) than in patients treated with surgery alone, and anxiety on the GAD-7 in 7.1 percent and insomnia in 7.2 percent (PMID 38837232); the oropharyngeal adenoid cystic carcinoma systematic review supplies the disease-trajectory context, documenting disease progression in 86 of 195 patients over the reviewed follow-up with distant metastases in 36 percent of those who progressed, which is the morbidity trajectory against which a mood consequence would be expected to accrue (PMID 42371638); and the SWOG S1609 DART phase II basket trial salivary gland tumour cohort supplies the contemporary interventional-design reference point against which the observational mood signal is bounded (PMID 42499790); recorded as documented association only, with the 15.5 percent figure carried as a symptom-screen prevalence rather than a depression diagnosis rate.
nexusClaim.causationStatus: Neither causation nor aggravation of a depressive disorder is established for any individual, and the instrument used is the central limitation: PHQ-8 is a screening instrument, and the located cohort reports the prevalence of ELEVATED SYMPTOMS rather than of diagnosed major depressive disorder, so the 15.5 percent figure cannot be read as a depression diagnosis rate and no anchor in this edge reports a structured diagnostic interview; the reported association is explicitly entangled with treatment, since the cohort finds mood and quality-of-life outcomes worse in patients who received adjuvant therapy, which means the mood burden may be treatment-induced, disease-induced, or both, and the design cannot apportion between them; the cohort is a survivorship population drawn from a single multidisciplinary clinic with 62 patients, which is a selected group; the systematic review reports progression and metastasis but reports no mood outcomes at all, so it contributes disease-severity context only and cannot be cited as mood evidence; and mood comorbidity after a head and neck malignancy is an expected finding in any cancer survivorship population, so the signal is not specific to salivary gland carcinoma and cannot distinguish a salivary-gland-specific route from a generic cancer-survivorship route. Individual claims require a structured diagnostic interview establishing a depressive disorder as distinct from adjustment disorder, grief, or a PHQ-8 screen alone, with dated onset relative to both diagnosis and treatment.

causalMechanism.primaryVector: The hypothesised vector is a compound psychosocial pathway in which a disfiguring and functionally consequential tumour in the highly visible face and neck produces body-image disturbance and social withdrawal, in which dysphagia and xerostomia restrict eating and social participation, and in which adjuvant radiotherapy and chemoradiation add a treatment-burden component; the pathway is named as compound rather than singular because the located cohort cannot apportion between tumour burden, treatment burden, and the functional consequences documented separately at this file's rank 1 and rank 3 edges, and no located anchor tests which component predominates.

evidentiaryProfile.conservativeRationale: Authored at ASSOCIATION_ONLY at survivorship-retrospective, PRISMA-systematic-review, and interventional-trial-cohort class, and deliberately at association-only strength even though the depressive-disorder target identity is among the most heavily used in the registry with eighty-nine registered incoming edges, because volume of precedent is not evidence for this particular route: the survivorship anchor is the only located source that measures mood directly with a named instrument and is registered together with its own treatment gradient and its own screening-instrument caveat (PMID 38837232); the systematic review is registered explicitly as disease-trajectory context that contains NO mood data, so that it is not misread as mood evidence (PMID 42371638); and the trial cohort supplies the contemporary design reference against which a future mood outcome analysis in salivary gland carcinoma should be read (PMID 42499790). Because the anchor reports a screening-tool prevalence rather than a diagnosis and because the treatment gradient is the dominant signal, the conservative standard keeps the edge at association only, states the screening-instrument limitation in the evidence gaps, and requires a structured diagnostic interview for any individual attribution.
evidentiaryProfile.evidenceGaps: The single direct mood anchor is a 62-patient single-clinic survivorship cohort self-designated level 4, reporting a 15.5 percent PHQ-8 symptom prevalence rather than a diagnosed-disorder rate, with no reported confidence interval and no reported structured interview; that cohort's mood findings are inseparable from its treatment groups, and its depression and anxiety figures are lower than its dysphagia and neck-pain figures, which is the opposite of the pattern usually reported in head and neck survivorship and suggests either genuine subsite-specificity or under-detection by screening; the systematic review contributes no mood data and is registered only as severity context; the basket-trial cohort is an interventional design that the located abstract does not report mood outcomes for, so it functions as a design pointer rather than as evidence for this edge; no located anchor reports mood outcomes stratified by salivary subsite, which is the only way a salivary-gland-specific route could be separated from a generic head-and-neck survivorship route; and no located anchor reports whether mood symptoms predated or followed treatment. Anxiety-disorder was reviewed and withheld as TARGET-EXHAUSTION given a 7.1 percent GAD-7 prevalence in the same cohort, which is below the threshold at which a separate edge would carry information the depression edge does not.
alternativeEtiologiesToRuleOut: Adjustment disorder, grief, or normal response to a disfiguring diagnosis, none of which is a depressive disorder
Treatment-induced mood burden from radiotherapy or chemoradiation rather than tumour-induced burden
Pre-existing depression or a psychiatric history predating the salivary gland malignancy
Dysphagia, xerostomia, and nutritional compromise as alternative drivers of low mood, documented separately at this file's rank 1 and rank 3 edges

evidenceGaps: The single direct mood anchor is a 62-patient single-clinic survivorship cohort self-designated level 4, reporting a 15.5 percent PHQ-8 symptom prevalence rather than a diagnosed-disorder rate, with no reported confidence interval and no reported structured interview; that cohort's mood findings are inseparable from its treatment groups, and its depression and anxiety figures are lower than its dysphagia and neck-pain figures, which is the opposite of the pattern usually reported in head and neck survivorship and suggests either genuine subsite-specificity or under-detection by screening; the systematic review contributes no mood data and is registered only as severity context; the basket-trial cohort is an interventional design that the located abstract does not report mood outcomes for, so it functions as a design pointer rather than as evidence for this edge; no located anchor reports mood outcomes stratified by salivary subsite, which is the only way a salivary-gland-specific route could be separated from a generic head-and-neck survivorship route; and no located anchor reports whether mood symptoms predated or followed treatment. Anxiety-disorder was reviewed and withheld as TARGET-EXHAUSTION given a 7.1 percent GAD-7 prevalence in the same cohort, which is below the threshold at which a separate edge would carry information the depression edge does not.
suggestions.rationale: Authoring registers this edge because the located cohort measured mood directly with a named instrument in a salivary gland malignancy population, which is a rarer thing to find than the cancer-depression literature generally, and because the treatment gradient in the same cohort is the operationally decisive detail: a veteran whose depression emerged after adjuvant radiotherapy has a materially different claim than one whose depression predates the tumour. The conservative framing states plainly that the anchor reports a screening prevalence rather than a diagnosis rate, registers the systematic review as containing no mood data so it cannot be over-read, and requires a structured diagnostic interview with dated onset before any individual attribution.

nexusClaim.associationBasis: Salivary gland carcinoma produces dry mouth through two independent routes, the disease route and the treatment route, and the located evidence documents the treatment route in depth: a mechanistic review of radiation-induced salivary gland dysfunction establishes that ionizing radiation damages salivary glands because of their proximity to common head and neck tumour sites, that damage results in loss of secretory function causing severe and chronic reductions in salivary flow, and that this leads directly to the patient-reported sensation of dry mouth termed xerostomia, with the described chronic mechanisms including decreased acinar differentiation markers, increased acinar cell proliferation, immune and inflammatory dysregulation, metabolic changes including increases in amino acids and reductions in glycolysis and oxidative phosphorylation, fibrosis, and dysregulated neuronal responses (PMID 38808518); a rapid evidence review of salivary gland disorders supplies the general clinical framing for salivary gland disease and its functional consequences (PMID 38905553); and the malignant parotid survivorship cohort establishes that this is a survivorship-relevant burden measured in a treated salivary gland malignancy population rather than a theoretical concern (PMID 38837232); recorded as documented association only, with the disease route carried as a separate hypothesized vector that no located anchor measures.
nexusClaim.causationStatus: Neither causation nor aggravation of xerostomia is established for any individual, and the two routes cannot be separated by the located evidence: the mechanistic review describes radiation damage in head and neck cancer populations generally and does not isolate salivary gland carcinoma as a subsite, so applying it to a salivary gland primary requires an inference the source does not make; that review also identifies the absence of a standard of care for permanent restoration of salivary function and describes the mechanisms as elusive, which is a statement about mechanism rather than about the robustness of the radiation-to-xerostomia association, which is nonetheless the more firmly established of the two routes; the rapid evidence review covers salivary gland disorders broadly and is not specific to malignancy; the survivorship cohort is registered for population relevance but the located abstract does not report a xerostomia instrument or prevalence, so it cannot serve as the quantitative anchor for this edge; and the disease route, in which a parotid or submandibular tumour replaces functioning gland tissue and a resection removes it, is documented in none of the three anchors and is carried here as a hypothesized second vector only. Individual claims require a dated salivary flow measurement or a validated xerostomia instrument, documented gland involvement and subsite, a dated radiotherapy timeline with dose and field coverage of the remaining salivary tissue, and separation of pre-treatment from post-treatment dryness.

causalMechanism.primaryVector: The hypothesised vector is destruction of functional salivary acinar tissue, either by direct tumour infiltration replacing gland parenchyma or by surgical resection removing it, and independently by the dose of ionizing radiation delivered to the contralateral and residual salivary tissue during adjuvant treatment, with radiation damage producing loss of secretory function and chronic reduction in salivary flow as the proximate mechanism and the resulting patient-reported dry mouth as the clinical expression; the treatment vector is the one the located evidence documents mechanistically, the disease-and-resection vector is the one carried as hypothesized because no located anchor measures it, and which predominates in an individual depends on subsite, laterality, and whether the contralateral gland lay within the irradiated field.

evidentiaryProfile.conservativeRationale: Authored at ASSOCIATION_ONLY at mechanistic-review, rapid-evidence-review, and survivorship-retrospective class, and it is the file's first edge to the xerostomia identity, which had zero registered incoming edges and zero outgoing edges before this batch: the mechanistic review is the anchor that supplies the actual causal chain from radiation exposure to acinar secretory loss to patient-reported xerostomia and is the only located source that describes the intermediate mechanism (PMID 38808518); the rapid evidence review supplies the general salivary-gland-disorder framing and is reused rather than duplicated, since its source entity pmid-38905553 was already registered in the master source registry and this edge therefore adds a reference use without adding a new source entity (PMID 38905553); and the survivorship cohort establishes population relevance in treated malignant parotid disease while being registered with the explicit caveat that its located abstract reports no xerostomia instrument or prevalence (PMID 38837232). Because the disease-and-resection route has no located anchor and because the treatment evidence is extrapolated from head and neck cohorts rather than from salivary gland primaries, the conservative standard keeps the edge at association only and splits the mechanism into a documented vector and a hypothesized one.
evidentiaryProfile.evidenceGaps: No located anchor measures xerostomia in a salivary gland carcinoma population specifically; the mechanistic review is a narrative review of radiation-induced damage in head and neck cancer and offers no incidence, no dose threshold, and no subsite-specific estimate, and it explicitly states the underlying mechanisms remain elusive and that there is no standard of care for permanent restoration of function; the rapid evidence review is a general salivary-gland-disorder synthesis and is not malignancy-specific; the survivorship cohort's located abstract reports dysphagia, depression, anxiety, neck pain, and insomnia but does NOT report a xerostomia measure, so it is registered for population relevance only and is explicitly not the quantitative anchor for this edge; no located anchor separates xerostomia caused by primary tumour infiltration from that caused by parotidectomy from that caused by radiotherapy, which is the central unresolved question; and no located anchor reports whether the contralateral gland was inside the irradiated field. Hearing-loss was reviewed and withheld as EVIDENCE-INSUFFICIENT because the located parotid literature reports facial nerve schwannomas and lateral skull base invasion rather than a quantified hearing-loss association, and facial nerve palsy was withheld as MISSING IDENTITY.
alternativeEtiologiesToRuleOut: Xerostomia from primary tumour infiltration of the gland or from surgical resection, separable only from the radiotherapy route by a dated pre-treatment assessment
Xerostomia from medications prescribed for comorbid conditions, including antidepressants and anticholinergics
Xerostomia from Sjögren syndrome or another independent salivary gland disorder
Dehydration or mouth breathing as alternative contributors to reported dry mouth

evidenceGaps: No located anchor measures xerostomia in a salivary gland carcinoma population specifically; the mechanistic review is a narrative review of radiation-induced damage in head and neck cancer and offers no incidence, no dose threshold, and no subsite-specific estimate, and it explicitly states the underlying mechanisms remain elusive and that there is no standard of care for permanent restoration of function; the rapid evidence review is a general salivary-gland-disorder synthesis and is not malignancy-specific; the survivorship cohort's located abstract reports dysphagia, depression, anxiety, neck pain, and insomnia but does NOT report a xerostomia measure, so it is registered for population relevance only and is explicitly not the quantitative anchor for this edge; no located anchor separates xerostomia caused by primary tumour infiltration from that caused by parotidectomy from that caused by radiotherapy, which is the central unresolved question; and no located anchor reports whether the contralateral gland was inside the irradiated field. Hearing-loss was reviewed and withheld as EVIDENCE-INSUFFICIENT because the located parotid literature reports facial nerve schwannomas and lateral skull base invasion rather than a quantified hearing-loss association, and facial nerve palsy was withheld as MISSING IDENTITY.
suggestions.rationale: Authoring registers this edge because the target identity had no registered incoming edge at all before this batch, because dry mouth is one of the most frequently claimed and least rigorously documented complaints in salivary gland malignancy survivorship, and because splitting the mechanism into a documented radiation vector and a hypothesized tumour-and-resection vector is what keeps the edge from overstating what the located evidence actually shows. The conservative framing reuses an already-registered source rather than duplicating it, registers the survivorship cohort as carrying no xerostomia measure, and requires a dated salivary flow or validated instrument result with a radiotherapy timeline before any individual attribution.

Retrospective study, malignant parotid tumour patients 2017-2023, level 4 evidence; abstract reports PROM prevalences for dysphagia, depression, anxiety, neck pain, and insomnia but NO xerostomia measure, so this reference supports population relevance and not the xerostomia association itself.

governanceNotes: D1 batch 81 (2026-09-27): three bounded association edges added - salivary-gland-cancer to dysphagia (rank 1, MECHANICAL_OR_COMPRESSIVE), salivary-gland-cancer to depressive-disorder (rank 2, PSYCHOPHYSIOLOGICAL), and salivary-gland-cancer to xerostomia (rank 3, POST_SURGICAL_OR_TREATMENT), all classified ASSOCIATION_ONLY with etiologicalConsensus NOT_ESTABLISHED, vaNexusProbabilityAlignment NOT_ASSERTED, and hypothesizedOnly:true. The primary anchor is the 62-patient malignant parotid survivorship cohort reporting dysphagia 32.3 percent, PHQ-8 elevation 15.5 percent, GAD-7 7.1 percent, neck pain 17.7 percent, and insomnia 7.2 percent, with significant quality-of-life gradients by adjuvant treatment (PMID 38837232); the oropharyngeal adenoid cystic carcinoma systematic review supplies subsite and progression context and contains no mood data (PMID 42371638); the radiation-induced salivary gland dysfunction review supplies the mechanistic chain to xerostomia (PMID 38808518); the salivary gland disorders rapid evidence review is reused from the existing registered source entity pmid-38905553 (PMID 38905553); and the DART SWOG S1609 basket-trial cohort is the contemporary design reference (PMID 42499790). The two documented confounds, adjuvant-treatment burden and the screening-instrument nature of the mood measure, are carried openly in the relevant edge rather than resolved.
